I.          INTRODUCTION AND OVERVIEW OF FILING

         As discussed below, the State Agreement Approach provides states with flexibility to
identify and sponsor transmission facilities needed to advance state public policy requirements,
while ensuring that the costs of those facilities are borne by customers in the sponsoring state or
states.8 The Ohio Federal Energy Advocate (“Ohio FEA”) has invoked that process on behalf of
the State of Ohio to facilitate transmission solutions that would support the Flagship Project, a
significant proposed development composed of substantial new load, associated new generation,
and new transmission infrastructure, as described further below.9 The Study Agreement submitted
herein represents an initial step in that process. It establishes the framework pursuant to which
PJM, as the independent regional transmission planner, will evaluate the Flagship Project on an
integrated basis and identify the transmission facilities needed to reliably accommodate the project
on the PJM transmission system.

        The Flagship Project is an integrated artificial intelligence (“AI”) data center, generation,
and transmission development centered at and around the former United States Department of
Energy (“DOE”) Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio. It has an initial 800
MW phase served under Ohio Power Company’s (“Ohio Power”) Data Center Tariff,10 and the
expansion being evaluated under the Study Agreement comprises approximately 9,570 MW of
additional load and 10,170 MW of gross new generation, supported by three proposed 765 kV
transmission lines and related infrastructure. As discussed further below,11 the project would
advance the State of Ohio’s public policy needs by (i) promoting adequate, reliable, safe, efficient,
nondiscriminatory, and reasonably priced retail electric service;12 (ii) protecting at-risk
populations by ensuring no other Ohio Power customers incur costs related to the Flagship
Project’s AI data center;13 and (iii) facilitating the State’s effectiveness in the global economy and
leadership in AI development.14 Further, SB Energy has committed to structuring and developing

service providers to perform the studies, allowing PJM to obtain the additional resources necessary

        At the same time, Commission acceptance of the Study Agreement would not constitute

studies are borne by the Flagship Project’s developer. PJM therefore respectfully requests that the
Commission accept the Study Agreement, effective September 25, 2026, as requested herein.

 II.         BACKGROUND

            A. The State Agreement Approach Framework

         The State Agreement Approach process25 provides a formal mechanism pursuant to which
PJM can respond to a request from one or more states that PJM study and consider transmission
facilities that would assist them in implementing Public Policy Requirements. Through this
process, PJM may consider state-sponsored transmission facilities, even if they are not needed to
address PJM’s required planning criteria specific to reliability, operational performance, or market
efficiency.26 The “basic tenets”27 of the State Agreement Approach process are that if the
requesting state(s) voluntarily chooses to sponsor any transmission facilities pursuant to the State
Agreement Approach process, that state(s) must agree that 100 percent of the costs associated with
such facilities will be recovered from customers in that state(s), and that no such costs may be
allocated to customers outside of the relevant state(s).28

        The State Agreement Approach mechanism is not a rigidly-defined process in the
Operating Agreement. Rather, the State Agreement Approach is intended to provide the flexibility
needed to accommodate the breadth of policies that a state might wish to pursue and to allow that
state to select the transmission solution(s) that best addresses its public policy needs. That is, the
State Agreement Approach allows authorized state governmental entities to determine how to
identify transmission facilities needed to address state Public Policy Requirements, including by
requesting a competitive solicitation process, but does not require that approach.29 The state(s)
responsible for the project’s cost allocation may also submit to PJM a prequalified entity to
construct, own, operate, and maintain the facilities.30 That choice is subject to exceptions in

III.        THE STUDY AGREEMENT ESTABLISHES THE FRAMEWORK FOR PJM’S
            EVALUATION OF THE OHIO FEA SAA REQUEST

        The Study Agreement sets forth just and reasonable terms for studying the consolidated
system integration of the load, transmission, and generation components of the Flagship Project.
The provisions of the Study Agreement are summarized below.

            A. Purpose and Limited Scope of the Study Agreement

         The Study Agreement provides that PJM will conduct an evaluation of the Flagship Project
on an integrated basis, including identifying the transmission facilities required to provide the
requested Network Integration Transmission Service (“NITS”) to serve the Proposed Flagship
Load and the facilities required for the proposed interconnection of the Proposed Flagship
Generation Facilities.44 PJM will assess whether the transmission facilities identified by AEP Ohio
are sufficient to support the requested level of NITS for the identified load and Capacity
Interconnection Rights (“CIRs”) for the identified generation and, if not, identify any additional
facilities needed to implement the Flagship Project.45 That evaluation will consider the
transmission system as a whole and will test the proposed facilities under the operating conditions

            C. PJM’s Study Scope and Evaluation Framework

                       1. Study Scope and Applicable Criteria

         Pursuant to the Study Agreement, PJM, as the independent regional transmission planner,
will be responsible for conducting an integrated, holistic technical evaluation of the Flagship
Project’s proposed load, proposed generation, and the transmission facilities already identified by
AEP Ohio to serve the load and interconnect the generation.55 PJM will assess how those
components operate together on the transmission system, whether the identified facilities can
accommodate the requested NITS and CIR levels under the study scenarios described below and,
if not, what additional transmission may be needed, at a planning level, to support the project and
address resulting reliability violations.56 PJM will conduct the studies in conformance with the
applicable provisions of PJM Manuals 14B (PJM Region Transmission Planning Process) and
Manual 14H (New Service Requests Cycle Process), and in accordance with the process set forth
in Schedule C of the Study Agreement.57 PJM will assess compliance with applicable NERC
Reliability Standards, PJM reliability criteria, and individual Transmission Owners’ planning
criteria.58

         Although the proposed generation associated with the Flagship Project will not be studied
through the PJM interconnection queue, the Study Agreement does not alter the substantive
reliability standards or planning criteria applicable to PJM’s evaluation of that generation.
Similarly, PJM will evaluate the transmission needs associated with the combined load, generation,
and transmission facilities contemplated by the Flagship Project, including whether the AEP Ohio-
identified transmission facilities are sufficient to address those needs, consistent with PJM’s
established transmission planning processes. Thus, while the Study Agreement establishes a
tailored process for evaluating the Flagship Project, PJM will apply the same substantive reliability
standards and planning criteria that govern its other transmission planning and interconnection
analyses.

                        2. Study Models and Evaluation Methodology

        The Study Agreement describes how PJM will establish the study models. PJM will

       PJM will evaluate the project using the “Most Credible Stressed Scenario(s)” described in
Schedule C of the Study Agreement. Those scenarios are based on the project information
provided, PJM’s historical experience, sound engineering judgment, Good Utility Practice, and
applicable governing requirements.65 The evaluation will consider the proposed load at the full
requested NITS level under various seasonal system conditions and the projected availability of
the proposed generation facilities, modeled as capacity resources at the requested CIR level.

       Using those scenarios, PJM will conduct load flow, short-circuit, and stability analyses
concurrently. The Study Agreement provides for those analyses to be performed under the study
assumptions and methodology set forth in Schedule C of the Study Agreement, with the anticipated
study durations and progress updates addressed separately in that Schedule.66

RTEP is ongoing, if PUCO does not act before expiration of the 120-day period, PJM must
determine whether any part of the studies needs to be updated to reflect then-current conditions

                    Study Agreement in Furtherance of the State of Ohio’s
                            State Agreement Approach Request

        This Study Agreement, dated September 25, 2026, is entered into by and among PJM
Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”), SE DC DevCo, LLC (“SE DC DevCo”), PORTS 2 Interconnect,
LLC (“PORTS 2 Interconnect”), Portsmouth Gas DevCo, LLC (“Portsmouth Gas DevCo”), and
AEP Ohio Transmission Company, Inc. (“AEP Ohio”) (each individually, a “Party,” and
collectively, the “Parties”) to establish the terms and conditions under which PJM will conduct the
studies necessary to respond to the State of Ohio’s request that PJM employ the State Agreement
Approach (“SAA”) process as set forth in the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“Operating Agreement”), Schedule 6, section 1.5.9 (“Regional
Transmission Expansion Planning Protocol - Procedure for Development of the Regional
Transmission Expansion Plan - State Agreement Approach”) (“SAA Process”).

                                           RECITALS

        WHEREAS, PJM, as the independent regional planner of the Regional Transmission
Expansion Plan (“RTEP”), is responsible for conducting transmission planning and
interconnection studies, including studies conducted under the SAA Process, pursuant to the rules
set forth in its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”), Operating Agreement, and business
manuals (collectively, “Governing Documents”);

        WHEREAS, on behalf of the State of Ohio, the Federal Energy Advocate of Ohio has
issued a letter to PJM dated June 15, 2026 (“Ohio SAA Request,” attached as Schedule A to this
Study Agreement) requesting that PJM initiate the SAA Process to facilitate “transmission
solutions that directly support public policy requirements”;

        WHEREAS, Ohio Revised Code 4928.02 establishes the state’s public policy for the
electric industry to promote reliable and reasonably priced electric service, competitive electricity
markets, consumer protection, grid modernization, innovation, and economic development (“Ohio
Public Policy Requirements”);

        WHEREAS, SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect, Portsmouth Gas DevCo, and AEP
Ohio have partnered to develop an integrated project consisting of the Proposed Flagship Load
Facilities, the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities and the Proposed Flagship Transmission
Facilities, each as defined in Schedule B to this Study Agreement (collectively, the “Flagship
Project”);

       WHEREAS, pursuant to the supplemental planning process set forth in Tariff, Attachment
M-3, AEP Ohio identified a customer service need associated with SE DC DevCo’s request for
800 MW of new demand at the new planned Mercury Substation of the Flagship Project as need
number AEP-2026-OH004, developed a transmission solution to serve that demand, and submitted
the associated transmission facilities for inclusion in its Local Plan as supplemental project ID
s3864.1-.6;



                                                                                              Page 1
          WHEREAS, the Ohio SAA Request (i) calls for PJM to initiate the SAA Process to
facilitate the transmission infrastructure necessary to support the Flagship Project; (ii) states that
SE DC DevCo has committed to bear all costs of transmission facilities and associated
infrastructure necessary to reliably interconnect the Flagship Project in furtherance of the Ohio
Public Policy Requirements; and (iii) acknowledges that the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio
(“PUCO”) will determine the appropriate state cost allocation and recovery mechanisms to assign
the costs of such transmission facilities directly to PORTS 2 Interconnect;

        WHEREAS, AEP Ohio has performed planning analyses of the proposed load associated
with the Flagship Project and has identified certain transmission facilities, as reflected in Schedule
B to this Study Agreement, that are necessary to reliably interconnect such load;

         WHEREAS, SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo have
asked PJM to perform all studies necessary to determine whether the transmission facilities
identified by AEP Ohio are sufficient, and to independently identify any additional transmission
facilities necessary to support reliable interconnection of, and service to, the Flagship Project as
more fully described in Schedule C (the “Studies”), and SE DC DevCo has agreed to assume sole
responsibility for the costs of the Studies;

        WHEREAS, AEP Ohio has agreed to construct the Proposed Flagship Transmission
Facilities based on SE DC DevCo’s, PORTS 2 Interconnect’s, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo’s
commitment to fund the transmission facilities to be identified by PJM through the planning
Studies; and

        WHEREAS, the Studies conducted pursuant to this Study Agreement are intended to
provide the technical basis for the State of Ohio to determine whether to proceed under the SAA
Process by entering into an agreement with PJM pursuant to Operating Agreement, Schedule 6,
section 1.5.9(a) (an “SAA Agreement”).

        NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of and subject to the mutual covenants contained
herein, the Parties agree as follows:

        PJM shall conduct the following Studies of the Flagship Project on an integrated basis:
(i) evaluation of the transmission facilities required to reliably provide Network Integration
Transmission Service (“NITS”) requested to serve the Flagship Project load described in Schedule
B and (ii) evaluation of the transmission facilities required for the proposed interconnection to the
PJM Transmission System of the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities described in Schedule
B. The Studies will include the evaluation of the Proposed Flagship Transmission Facilities
identified in Schedule B, including the 765 kV transmission facilities identified by AEP Ohio, to
determine whether such facilities are sufficient to support the requested level of NITS and Capacity
Interconnection Rights (“CIRs”); if not, to identify any additional transmission facilities required
to implement the Flagship Project at the requested NITS and CIR levels through the assessment of
the most credible stressed scenario(s) from both load and generation perspectives to enable the
reliable interconnection of the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities at the requested CIR level
and enable reliable service to the Proposed Flagship Load Facilities at the requested NITS level,
as set forth in Schedule B to this Agreement.

     1.     Milestones. The Parties shall endeavor to satisfy the milestones set forth in Schedule
C of this Study Agreement. Milestones set forth in Schedule C may be extended by mutual
agreement of the Parties. Any extension of a milestone that will affect the anticipated in-service
date of the Flagship Project shall be presented to the PJM Transmission Expansion Advisory
Committee and posted on PJM’s website.

    2. PJM Discretion. PJM will conduct the Studies in compliance with the applicable
provisions of Manual 14B (PJM Region Transmission Planning Process) and Manual 14H (New
Service Requests Cycle Process), and in accordance with the Study Process and Milestone
Schedule set forth in Schedule C. PJM shall have sole discretion to determine the scope, study
methodology, study criteria, and modeling assumptions utilized during the Studies and may
modify any such scope, methodology, criteria, or modeling assumptions it deems necessary to
maintain system reliability, ensure accurate study results, or reflect changes in planning
assumptions, system conditions, or applicable reliability criteria; provided that PJM shall promptly
inform SE DC DevCo of any such modifications that deviate from specific study criteria,
assumptions, and methodology expressly set forth in this Agreement, including the information

                     STUDY PROCESS AND MILESTONE SCHEDULE

Evaluation of Flagship Project

1. Completeness Review: Upon execution of this Study Agreement by all Parties, PJM shall
have five (5) days to identify any additional information need to complete the Studies. The Data
Deficiency Review described below will commence immediately if PJM indicates it does not
require additional information or will proceed once PJM acknowledges receipt of any necessary
information it has requested.

2. Data Deficiency Review: Upon completion of the Completeness Review, PJM will perform a
deficiency review of all information and data supplied by SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect,
and Portsmouth Gas DevCo (“Study Data”). The Study Data will be evaluated against the
requirements described in the PJM Tariff, Operating Agreement, and Manual 14H to ensure the
Study Data sufficiently describes the Flagship Project for purposes of the Studies. If PJM
determines, in its sole discretion, that additional Study Data is required, SE DC DevCo, PORTS
2 Interconnect, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo will have ten (10) days to supply such information.
This process shall continue until PJM determines that the Study Data is sufficient to perform the
Studies. PJM will complete the initial and any subsequent data reviews within fifteen (15) days
after receipt of the completed or revised Study Data.

3. Base Case Development and Review. PJM will provide any individual at SE DC DevCo,
PORTS 2 Interconnect, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo, and AEP with approved CEII clearance with
the draft study models proposed for use in the Studies, including the applicable power-flow, short
circuit, and stability models, for review and comment. SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect,
and Portsmouth Gas DevCo will have thirty (30) days to review and provide any comments.
PJM will consider SE DC DevCo’s, PORTS 2 Interconnect’s, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo’s
comments and provide the final study models concurrently with the commencement of the
applicable Studies.

4. Most Credible Stressed Scenario(s): PJM will evaluate the Flagship Project using a “Most
Credible Stressed Scenario(s),” meaning the most credible stressed system and operating
conditions based on information provided by SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect, Portsmouth
Gas DevCo, and AEP Ohio, PJM’s historical experience, sound engineering judgment, Good
Utility Practice, and applicable PJM Tariff, Operating Agreement, and Manual requirements. In
developing the Most Credible Stressed Scenario(s), PJM will evaluate the Proposed Flagship
Load Facilities at the full NITS level under various seasonal PJM system conditions and based
on the projected availability of the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities. For purposes of
such evaluation, PJM will model the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities using the
applicable class average expected forced outage rate to account for simultaneous outages during
major overhauls and similar conditions, and will reflect the obligations of the Proposed Flagship
Generation Facilities as a capacity resource at the requested CIR level.
5. Studies: Following PJM’s completion of the Completeness and Data Deficiency Reviews
described above, PJM will conduct the Studies using the Most Credible Stressed Scenario(s)

 described above. The Studies will consist of a load flow analysis, short circuit analysis, and
stability analysis, which PJM will conduct concurrently. PJM anticipates completing the load
flow analysis in not more than sixty (60) days, the short circuit analysis in not more than sixty
(60) days, and the stability analysis in not more than one hundred and twenty (120) days. PJM
will provide regular updates as study results become available during the power flow study, short
circuit and stability study stages. To provide SE DC DevCo and AEP with an early update on
study progress, PJM will conduct the stability analysis starting with the most extreme
contingencies first and will share the results and any identified reliability violations upon
completion of these extreme contingencies. PJM will similarly alert SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2
Interconnect, Portsmouth Gas DevCo, AEP, and any Affected System Operators and affected

including, as applicable, the base cases, project-modified cases, contingency and monitored-
element files, short circuit models, dynamic models and data, model assumptions and
modifications, and final solved cases. PJM will not provide training on the use or interpretation
of these study materials for the Parties or their consultants.

7. Actions Following Reliability Report: Within thirty (30) days following receipt of the
Reliability Report, SE DC DevCo shall notify PJM in writing that it elects to either:
    1. terminate this Study Agreement;
    2. request that PJM proceed with the identification of Required Transmission Upgrades
        (defined below) and prepare a System Upgrade Report (defined below); or,
    3. revise the levels of requested service, or modify the equipment specifications, equipment
        configurations, or other specifications listed in Schedule B, in which case PJM will
        determine whether and to what extent any of the Studies must be repeated in accordance
        with the Revised Study process (described below).

8. Revised Study and Revised Reliability Report: If SE DC DevCo elects to modify the
Flagship Project or requested service pursuant to Section 6 of this Schedule C, SE DC DevCo
shall provide PJM with all Study Data necessary to evaluate the proposed modification. PJM
will determine, in its sole discretion, whether and to what extent the modification requires PJM
to repeat or modify any portion of the Studies (the “Revised Study”). Any Revised Study will be
performed in accordance with the applicable study assumptions, methodologies, and
requirements set forth in this Schedule C. PJM anticipates completing the Revised Study within




                                                                                         Page 18
 sixty (60) days following its determination that the Study Data necessary to perform the Revised
Study is sufficient; provided, however, that the time required to complete the Revised Study may
vary depending on the nature and complexity of the proposed modifications.

Upon completion of the Revised Study, PJM will prepare and provide to the Parties and PUCO a
revised Reliability Report reflecting the results of the Revised Study (“Revised Reliability
Report”). The Revised Reliability Report will identify the reliability violations, if any, resulting
from the Revised Study and whether PJM has determined that an Affected System Study is

Within thirty (30) days following receipt of the Revised Reliability Report, SE DC DevCo shall

below); or (ii) terminate this Study Agreement.

9. Identification of Required Transmission Upgrades and System Upgrade Report: If SE
DC DevCo elects to proceed following receipt of the Reliability Report or Revised Reliability
Report, as applicable, PJM will coordinate with AEP Ohio, Affected System Operators, and
affected Transmission Owners as necessary, to identify the transmission facilities and upgrades
required to interconnect the Flagship Project and solve all reliability violations identified in the
applicable Reliability Report or Revised Reliability Report (the “Required Transmission
Upgrades”).

Following identification of the Required Transmission Upgrades, PJM will prepare and provide
to the Parties and PUCO a System Upgrade Report identifying the Required Transmission
Upgrades. PJM estimates completing the System Upgrade Report within thirty (30) days
following SE DC DevCo’s election to proceed, subject to the timely receipt of information
required from AEP Ohio, any other affected Transmission Owner(s) and/or Affected System
Operator(s). PJM shall use best efforts to coordinate with affected Transmission Owner(s)
and/or Affected System Operator(s) as expeditiously as possible; provided, that the Parties
acknowledge that PJM cannot unilaterally control the timing of Affected System Studies, which
are coordinated with neighboring regions and transmission owners; the time necessary to
complete Affected Systems studies will vary depending on the magnitude and nature of identified
reliability violations or impacts, if any.

                    Study Agreement in Furtherance of the State of Ohio’s
                            State Agreement Approach Request

        This Study Agreement, dated September 25, 2026, is entered into by and among PJM
Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”), SE DC DevCo, LLC (“SE DC DevCo”), PORTS 2 Interconnect,
LLC (“PORTS 2 Interconnect”), Portsmouth Gas DevCo, LLC (“Portsmouth Gas DevCo”), and
AEP Ohio Transmission Company, Inc. (“AEP Ohio”) (each individually, a “Party,” and
collectively, the “Parties”) to establish the terms and conditions under which PJM will conduct the
studies necessary to respond to the State of Ohio’s request that PJM employ the State Agreement
Approach (“SAA”) process as set forth in the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of PJM
Interconnection, L.L.C. (“Operating Agreement”), Schedule 6, section 1.5.9 (“Regional
Transmission Expansion Planning Protocol - Procedure for Development of the Regional
Transmission Expansion Plan - State Agreement Approach”) (“SAA Process”).

                                           RECITALS

        WHEREAS, PJM, as the independent regional planner of the Regional Transmission
Expansion Plan (“RTEP”), is responsible for conducting transmission planning and
interconnection studies, including studies conducted under the SAA Process, pursuant to the rules
set forth in its Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”), Operating Agreement, and business
manuals (collectively, “Governing Documents”);

        WHEREAS, on behalf of the State of Ohio, the Federal Energy Advocate of Ohio has
issued a letter to PJM dated June 15, 2026 (“Ohio SAA Request,” attached as Schedule A to this
Study Agreement) requesting that PJM initiate the SAA Process to facilitate “transmission
solutions that directly support public policy requirements”;

        WHEREAS, Ohio Revised Code 4928.02 establishes the state’s public policy for the
electric industry to promote reliable and reasonably priced electric service, competitive electricity
markets, consumer protection, grid modernization, innovation, and economic development (“Ohio
Public Policy Requirements”);

        WHEREAS, SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect, Portsmouth Gas DevCo, and AEP
Ohio have partnered to develop an integrated project consisting of the Proposed Flagship Load
Facilities, the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities and the Proposed Flagship Transmission
Facilities, each as defined in Schedule B to this Study Agreement (collectively, the “Flagship
Project”);

       WHEREAS, pursuant to the supplemental planning process set forth in Tariff, Attachment
M-3, AEP Ohio identified a customer service need associated with SE DC DevCo’s request for 800
MW of new demand at the new planned Mercury Substation of the Flagship Project as need
number AEP-2026-OH004, developed a transmission solution to serve that demand, and submitted
the associated transmission facilities for inclusion in its Local Plan as supplemental project ID
s3864.1-.6;
          WHEREAS, the Ohio SAA Request (i) calls for PJM to initiate the SAA Process to
facilitate the transmission infrastructure necessary to support the Flagship Project; (ii) states that
SE DC DevCo has committed to bear all costs of transmission facilities and associated
infrastructure necessary to reliably interconnect the Flagship Project in furtherance of the Ohio
Public Policy Requirements; and (iii) acknowledges that the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio
(“PUCO”) will determine the appropriate state cost allocation and recovery mechanisms to assign
the costs of such transmission facilities directly to PORTS 2 Interconnect;

        WHEREAS, AEP Ohio has performed planning analyses of the proposed load associated
with the Flagship Project and has identified certain transmission facilities, as reflected in Schedule
B to this Study Agreement, that are necessary to reliably interconnect such load;

         WHEREAS, SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo have
asked PJM to perform all studies necessary to determine whether the transmission facilities
identified by AEP Ohio are sufficient, and to independently identify any additional transmission
facilities necessary to support reliable interconnection of, and service to, the Flagship Project as
more fully described in Schedule C (the “Studies”), and SE DC DevCo has agreed to assume sole
responsibility for the costs of the Studies;

        WHEREAS, AEP Ohio has agreed to construct the Proposed Flagship Transmission
Facilities based on SE DC DevCo’s, PORTS 2 Interconnect’s, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo’s
commitment to fund the transmission facilities to be identified by PJM through the planning
Studies; and

        WHEREAS, the Studies conducted pursuant to this Study Agreement are intended to
provide the technical basis for the State of Ohio to determine whether to proceed under the SAA
Process by entering into an agreement with PJM pursuant to Operating Agreement, Schedule 6,
section 1.5.9(a) (an “SAA Agreement”).

        NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of and subject to the mutual covenants contained
herein, the Parties agree as follows:

        PJM shall conduct the following Studies of the Flagship Project on an integrated basis:
(i) evaluation of the transmission facilities required to reliably provide Network Integration
Transmission Service (“NITS”) requested to serve the Flagship Project load described in Schedule
B and (ii) evaluation of the transmission facilities required for the proposed interconnection to the
PJM Transmission System of the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities described in Schedule B.
The Studies will include the evaluation of the Proposed Flagship Transmission Facilities identified
in Schedule B, including the 765 kV transmission facilities identified by AEP Ohio, to determine
whether such facilities are sufficient to support the requested level of NITS and Capacity
Interconnection Rights (“CIRs”); if not, to identify any additional transmission facilities required
to implement the Flagship Project at the requested NITS and CIR levels through the assessment of
the most credible stressed scenario(s) from both load and generation perspectives to enable the
reliable interconnection of the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities at the requested CIR level
and enable reliable service to the Proposed Flagship Load Facilities at the requested NITS level, as
set forth in Schedule B to this Agreement.
     1.     Milestones. The Parties shall endeavor to satisfy the milestones set forth in Schedule C
of this Study Agreement. Milestones set forth in Schedule C may be extended by mutual
agreement of the Parties. Any extension of a milestone that will affect the anticipated in-service
date of the Flagship Project shall be presented to the PJM Transmission Expansion Advisory
Committee and posted on PJM’s website.

    2. PJM Discretion. PJM will conduct the Studies in compliance with the applicable
provisions of Manual 14B (PJM Region Transmission Planning Process) and Manual 14H (New
Service Requests Cycle Process), and in accordance with the Study Process and Milestone
Schedule set forth in Schedule C. PJM shall have sole discretion to determine the scope, study
methodology, study criteria, and modeling assumptions utilized during the Studies and may
modify any such scope, methodology, criteria, or modeling assumptions it deems necessary to
maintain system reliability, ensure accurate study results, or reflect changes in planning
assumptions, system conditions, or applicable reliability criteria; provided that PJM shall promptly
inform SE DC DevCo of any such modifications that deviate from specific study criteria,
assumptions, and methodology expressly set forth in this Agreement, including the information
contained in Schedules B and C to this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, PJM, as the
independent Transmission Planner, shall not perform any study that deviates from any applicable
reliability criteria or compromises the safety and reliability of the bulk electric system

    3.      Timing. PJM shall conduct the Studies with all due diligence and according to the
timelines and procedures set forth in this Study Agreement. The results of the Studies performed
under this Study Agreement, as reflected in the System Upgrade Report described in Schedule C,
may be relied upon as the basis for inclusion of the Required Transmission Upgrades (as defined in
Schedule C) in the PJM RTEP, provided that the PUCO takes the action required under Article 23
of this Study Agreement no later than 120 days following PJM’s delivery of a System Upgrade
Report. If the PUCO has not taken such action before the expiration of such 120 day period, PJM
will determine whether any portion of the Studies must be updated to reflect then-current system
conditions before PJM initiates the process for inclusion of the Required Transmission Upgrades in
the RTEP. If PJM determines that an update is necessary, SE DC DevCo shall reimburse PJM for all
actual costs associated with such study update pursuant to Article 9 of this Agreement. This period
may be extended by written agreement of the Parties. If there are opportunities to accelerate the
study timeline at additional expense to SE DC DevCo, PJM shall promptly inform SE DC DevCo.

     4.    Cooperation. To achieve the desired milestones, SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2
Interconnect, Portsmouth Gas DevCo, and AEP Ohio shall cooperate with PJM and timely provide
all information, data, assumptions, models, and other materials reasonably requested by PJM that
are necessary to conduct the Studies.

    5.       Verification. PJM shall be entitled to rely on any information, data, documents,
representations, or other materials provided by SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect, Portsmouth
Gas DevCo, or AEP Ohio or on SE DC DevCo’s, PORTS 2 Interconnect’s, Portsmouth Gas
DevCo’s, or AEP Ohio’s behalf without independent verification. PJM shall have no duty or
obligation to investigate, audit, verify, supplement or otherwise assess the accuracy, completeness,
reliability or sufficiency of the aforementioned information.
     6.     Changes to the Flagship Project While the Studies are in Progress. If SE DC DevCo,
PORTS 2 Interconnect, or Portsmouth Gas DevCo requests any material changes to the Flagship
Project specifications set forth in Schedule B after commencement of the Studies but before the
Studies are concluded, PJM may, in its sole discretion, determine whether any portion of the
Studies must be modified or repeated or whether additional funding commitments are required.
Prior to modifying or repeating any portion of the Studies or requiring any additional studies or
additional funding commitments, PJM will promptly inform SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2
Interconnect, Portsmouth Gas DevCo, and AEP Ohio whether the requested change(s) and
resulting modifications to the Studies would extend or delay the applicable milestones set forth in
Schedule C. Any modification to the Flagship Project or requested service following issuance of
the Reliability Report shall be governed by the Revised Study process set forth in Schedule C.

    7.     Study Process. Following completion of the data completeness and deficiency review
processes described in Schedule C, PJM will conduct the Studies necessary to evaluate the
Flagship Project for potential reliability violations in accordance with Article 2 and the study
process set forth in Schedule C. The Studies will evaluate the Flagship Project described in
Schedule B using the study assumptions, methodologies, and scenarios described in Schedule C.
The results of the Studies will be documented in the applicable reports identified in Schedule C.
The Studies, including any Revised Study, will be performed to yield planning-level estimates of
the transmission facilities needed to form an SAA Agreement. It remains the sole responsibility of
SE DC DevCo to identify the project specifications and other project-specific information set forth
in Schedule B that PJM should use as inputs in performing the Studies or a Revised Study.

    8.      Study Limitations. The Studies shall only be valid for the assumptions and project
specifications set forth in Schedules B and C, as may be amended from time to time by agreement
of the Parties consistent with Articles 2 and 6 of this Agreement. This Study Agreement shall not
be read to encompass the selection of any projects or designated entities, the establishment of any
cost allocations, or the grant of any specific transmission rights.

    9.      Study Fee. SE DC DevCo shall pay a $500,000 study deposit upon execution of this
Study Agreement for the integrated Studies required under this Study Agreement to evaluate the
Flagship Project. An additional $500,000 study deposit is required upon submission of new
specifications for a Revised Study. Actual study costs may exceed the deposit. Notwithstanding
the amount of the study deposit, SE DC DevCo shall reimburse PJM for all the actual cost of the
Studies. PJM will endeavor to identify any additional costs within thirty (30) days of completing
the Studies or a Revised Study. If PJM sends SE DC DevCo notification of additional study costs,
then SE DC DevCo must pay all additional study costs within thirty (30) days (or, if the 30th day is
not a Business Day, then the next Business Day) of PJM sending the notification of such additional
study costs. If the Study Agreement is terminated, or the Parties and PUCO execute an SAA
Agreement for the Flagship Project pursuant to Operating Agreement, Schedule 6, section 1.5.9,
PJM will return any unused portion of the study deposit.

   10.     Base Case Assumptions. PJM will use the 2025 RTEP base case reflecting 2030 system
conditions, including any PJM Board-approved modifications as of the execution of this Study
Agreement, in performing the Studies and any Revised Study.
     11.     Reliability Standards. The Studies will assess compliance with (i) NERC Reliability
Standards (which include Applicable Regional Entity reliability standards); (ii) PJM reliability
criteria; and (iii) Individual Transmission Owner planning criteria as filed in FERC Form No. 715
prior to the 2025 RTEP cycle and posted on the PJM website.

    12.    Confidentiality. The Parties acknowledge that information relating to the Studies, any
Revised Study, and resulting transmission planning process may be disclosed in filings before the
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”), the PUCO, or otherwise as necessary to
perform any of the studies described in this Study Agreement, or implement the resulting
transmission solutions. Except as required for those purposes or otherwise required by law, each
Party, and the Parties’ Third-Party Contractors (as defined below), shall maintain the
confidentiality of any non-public commercial, technical, or Critical Energy Infrastructure
Information (“CEII”) received from another Party in connection with this Study Agreement.

    13.    Third-Party Contractors. PJM may, in its sole discretion, engage or subcontract with
one or more third-party contractors, subcontractors, consultants, affiliates, or service providers to
perform the Studies (“Third-Party Contractors”).

    14.     Limitation of Liability. In no event will PJM, or other subcontractors employed by PJM
be liable for indirect, special, incidental, punitive, or consequential damages of any kind including
loss of profits, whether under this Study Agreement or otherwise. Nor shall PJM, or subcontractors
employed by PJM be liable for any delay in delivery of, or of the non-performance or delay in
performance of, PJM’s obligations under this Study Agreement. Neither Party has any monetary
liability under this Study Agreement beyond the payment of the Study Fee set forth in paragraph 9.

    15.     Effective Date. This Study Agreement shall become effective on the date it is executed
by all Parties, or such other date as specified by FERC.

    16.    Capitalized Terms. Unless otherwise defined in this Study Agreement, all capitalized
terms herein shall have the meaning set forth in the definition of such terms as stated in the PJM
Tariff or Operating Agreement.

    17.     Notice. Any notice, demand, or request required or permitted to be given by any Party

   22.     Breach.

           a.      Milestones. A breach of this Study Agreement shall include a failure to satisfy a

           b.      Notice. A Party not in breach shall give written notice of an event of breach to

           c.      Cure of Breach or Termination Pursuant to Breach. The breaching Party may

    23.     Term and Termination. Unless otherwise terminated consistent with this Study

               d.     FERC Approval. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement,

   24.    Governing Law, Regulatory Authority, and Rules. The validity, interpretation, and

   25.     No Third-Party Beneficiaries. Except as otherwise provided herein, this Study
Agreement is not intended to and does not create rights, remedies, or benefits of any character

and the obligations herein assumed are solely for the use and benefit of the Parties.

    26.    Multiple Counterparts. This Study Agreement may be executed in two or more
counterparts, each of which is deemed an original but all of which constitute one and the same

an association, joint venture, agency relationship, or partnership between the Parties or to impose

    28.     Severability. If any provision or portion of this Study Agreement shall for any reason

independent, (ii) the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to restore insofar as practicable the

     29.     Reservation of Rights. Nothing in this Study Agreement shall limit the rights of the

                     STUDY PROCESS AND MILESTONE SCHEDULE

Evaluation of Flagship Project

1. Completeness Review: Upon execution of this Study Agreement by all Parties, PJM shall
have five (5) days to identify any additional information need to complete the Studies. The Data
Deficiency Review described below will commence immediately if PJM indicates it does not
require additional information or will proceed once PJM acknowledges receipt of any necessary
information it has requested.

2. Data Deficiency Review: Upon completion of the Completeness Review, PJM will perform a
deficiency review of all information and data supplied by SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect,
and Portsmouth Gas DevCo (“Study Data”). The Study Data will be evaluated against the
requirements described in the PJM Tariff, Operating Agreement, and Manual 14H to ensure the
Study Data sufficiently describes the Flagship Project for purposes of the Studies. If PJM
determines, in its sole discretion, that additional Study Data is required, SE DC DevCo, PORTS
2 Interconnect, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo will have ten (10) days to supply such information.
This process shall continue until PJM determines that the Study Data is sufficient to perform the
Studies. PJM will complete the initial and any subsequent data reviews within fifteen (15) days
after receipt of the completed or revised Study Data.

3. Base Case Development and Review. PJM will provide any individual at SE DC DevCo,
PORTS 2 Interconnect, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo, and AEP with approved CEII clearance
with the draft study models proposed for use in the Studies, including the applicable power-flow,
short circuit, and stability models, for review and comment. SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2
Interconnect, and Portsmouth Gas DevCo will have thirty (30) days to review and provide any
comments. PJM will consider SE DC DevCo’s, PORTS 2 Interconnect’s, and Portsmouth Gas
DevCo’s comments and provide the final study models concurrently with the commencement of
the applicable Studies.

4. Most Credible Stressed Scenario(s): PJM will evaluate the Flagship Project using a “Most
Credible Stressed Scenario(s),” meaning the most credible stressed system and operating
conditions based on information provided by SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect, Portsmouth
Gas DevCo, and AEP Ohio, PJM’s historical experience, sound engineering judgment, Good
Utility Practice, and applicable PJM Tariff, Operating Agreement, and Manual requirements. In
developing the Most Credible Stressed Scenario(s), PJM will evaluate the Proposed Flagship
Load Facilities at the full NITS level under various seasonal PJM system conditions and based
on the projected availability of the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities. For purposes of
such evaluation, PJM will model the Proposed Flagship Generation Facilities using the
applicable class average expected forced outage rate to account for simultaneous outages during
major overhauls and similar conditions, and will reflect the obligations of the Proposed Flagship
Generation Facilities as a capacity resource at the requested CIR level.
5. Studies: Following PJM’s completion of the Completeness and Data Deficiency Reviews
described above, PJM will conduct the Studies using the Most Credible Stressed Scenario(s)
 described above. The Studies will consist of a load flow analysis, short circuit analysis, and
stability analysis, which PJM will conduct concurrently. PJM anticipates completing the load
flow analysis in not more than sixty (60) days, the short circuit analysis in not more than sixty
(60) days, and the stability analysis in not more than one hundred and twenty (120) days. PJM
will provide regular updates as study results become available during the power flow study, short
circuit and stability study stages. To provide SE DC DevCo and AEP with an early update on
study progress, PJM will conduct the stability analysis starting with the most extreme
contingencies first and will share the results and any identified reliability violations upon
completion of these extreme contingencies. PJM will similarly alert SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2
Interconnect, Portsmouth Gas DevCo, AEP, and any Affected System Operators and affected
Transmission Owners as soon as practicable if it appears an Affected Systems study is necessary.
However, PJM’s final assessment of the stability results will only be provided with the
Reliability Report upon completion of the entire set of dynamic stability studies.

6. Reliability Report: Following completion of all Studies, PJM will prepare and provide to the
Parties and PUCO a report identifying the reliability violations, if any, identified through the
Studies (the “Reliability Report”) and, expressed as percentages of the total number of such
violations, the share of such violations attributable to the proposed load and the proposed
generation, respectively. The Reliability Report will also identify whether PJM has determined
that an Affected Systems Study is required. The Reliability Report will not identify the
transmission facilities or upgrades necessary to address the identified reliability violations.
Concurrently with the Reliability Report, PJM will provide to the individuals with approved
CEII clearances at each of the Parties, complete copies of all study models and associated data
files used to perform the Studies and produce the results reflected in the Reliability Report,
including, as applicable, the base cases, project-modified cases, contingency and monitored-
element files, short circuit models, dynamic models and data, model assumptions and
modifications, and final solved cases. PJM will not provide training on the use or interpretation
of these study materials for the Parties or their consultants.

7. Actions Following Reliability Report: Within thirty (30) days following receipt of the
Reliability Report, SE DC DevCo shall notify PJM in writing that it elects to either:
    1. terminate this Study Agreement;
    2. request that PJM proceed with the identification of Required Transmission Upgrades
       (defined below) and prepare a System Upgrade Report (defined below); or,
    3. revise the levels of requested service, or modify the equipment specifications, equipment
       configurations, or other specifications listed in Schedule B, in which case PJM will
       determine whether and to what extent any of the Studies must be repeated in accordance
       with the Revised Study process (described below).

8. Revised Study and Revised Reliability Report: If SE DC DevCo elects to modify the
Flagship Project or requested service pursuant to Section 6 of this Schedule C, SE DC DevCo
shall provide PJM with all Study Data necessary to evaluate the proposed modification. PJM
will determine, in its sole discretion, whether and to what extent the modification requires PJM
to repeat or modify any portion of the Studies (the “Revised Study”). Any Revised Study will be
performed in accordance with the applicable study assumptions, methodologies, and
requirements set forth in this Schedule C. PJM anticipates completing the Revised Study within
 sixty (60) days following its determination that the Study Data necessary to perform the Revised
Study is sufficient; provided, however, that the time required to complete the Revised Study may
vary depending on the nature and complexity of the proposed modifications.

Upon completion of the Revised Study, PJM will prepare and provide to the Parties and PUCO a
revised Reliability Report reflecting the results of the Revised Study (“Revised Reliability
Report”). The Revised Reliability Report will identify the reliability violations, if any, resulting
from the Revised Study and whether PJM has determined that an Affected System Study is
required. The Revised Reliability Report will not identify the transmission facilities or upgrades
necessary to address the identified reliability violations.

Within thirty (30) days following receipt of the Revised Reliability Report, SE DC DevCo shall
notify PJM in writing whether it elects to: (i) proceed with the identification of the Required
Transmission Upgrades (defined below) and preparation of the System Upgrade Report (defined
below); or (ii) terminate this Study Agreement.

9. Identification of Required Transmission Upgrades and System Upgrade Report: If SE
DC DevCo elects to proceed following receipt of the Reliability Report or Revised Reliability
Report, as applicable, PJM will coordinate with AEP Ohio, Affected System Operators, and
affected Transmission Owners as necessary, to identify the transmission facilities and upgrades
required to interconnect the Flagship Project and solve all reliability violations identified in the
applicable Reliability Report or Revised Reliability Report (the “Required Transmission
Upgrades”).

Following identification of the Required Transmission Upgrades, PJM will prepare and provide
to the Parties and PUCO a System Upgrade Report identifying the Required Transmission
Upgrades. PJM estimates completing the System Upgrade Report within thirty (30) days
following SE DC DevCo’s election to proceed, subject to the timely receipt of information
required from AEP Ohio, any other affected Transmission Owner(s) and/or Affected System
Operator(s). PJM shall use best efforts to coordinate with affected Transmission Owner(s)
and/or Affected System Operator(s) as expeditiously as possible; provided, that the Parties
acknowledge that PJM cannot unilaterally control the timing of Affected System Studies, which
are coordinated with neighboring regions and transmission owners; the time necessary to
complete Affected Systems studies will vary depending on the magnitude and nature of
identified reliability violations or impacts, if any.
